name: Interventions to increase heat pump adoption in UK homes
question: What interventions are effective at increasing heat pump adoption in UK homes?

plan.title: Interventions to increase heat pump adoption in UK homes
plan.question: What interventions are effective at increasing heat pump adoption in UK homes?
scoping_notes: Intervention focus: policies, incentives, advice, financing, regulation, service models or other measures intended to increase heat pump adoption.
Outcome focus: heat pump adoption, installation, uptake, purchase intention or closely related conversion decisions.
screening_criteria: Include interventions targeting heat pump adoption or uptake.
Include empirical, evaluation, modelling or policy-analysis evidence.
Include outcomes on adoption, installation, uptake or purchase intention.
Exclude documents only about heat pump technical performance.
Exclude documents with no intervention-outcome evidence.
Exclude opinion pieces without evidence or analysis.

component_rationale.group: Included to organise extracted findings by intervention type for a policy-useful synthesis.
component_rationale.select: Included because this is an intervention-effectiveness question, so a subset of relevant documents should be selected for structured extraction.
component_rationale.extract: Included because intervention-outcome findings can be captured in the schema for effects on heat pump adoption.
component_rationale.characterise: Included to map intervention types, evidence coverage, UK relevance and gaps across the corpus.
component_rationale.screen_stage2: Included because standard depth supports a full-text precision check before synthesis.

assumptions: The review is about interventions intended to increase domestic heat pump adoption, not technical heat pump performance.
UK homes includes owner-occupied, private rented and social housing unless later narrowed.
Adoption includes installation, uptake, purchase intention or conversion from fossil-fuel heating where the source links it to likely uptake.
No publication date limit is imposed unless you request a recency window.
Grey-literature publisher geography is not restricted; UK relevance will be assessed from the document text.
The run may find evaluation evidence, modelling, surveys and policy analyses; only documents with evidence relevant to adoption will be retained.
